subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Prove that the product of the perpendiculars from (α,β) to the pair of lines ax²+2hxy+by²=0 is |aα²+2hαβ+bβ²| : √((a−b)²+4h²).

mark_split.label: Split the pair and match coefficients

recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — say what form you split the pair into, and what the numerator turns into.

steps.label: Split the pair and match coefficients
steps.margin_note: First mark. Split the pair in the general homogeneous form l₁x + m₁y, which is the form the perpendicular-distance formula expects.
lines: On equating like term coeff., we get
a = l₁l₂,   b = m₁m₂,   2h = l₁m₂ + l₂m₁

recall.must_convey: That the pair is split as (l₁x + m₁y)(l₂x + m₂y) with a = l₁l₂, b = m₁m₂, 2h = l₁m₂ + l₂m₁.
accept: split the pair into two lines through the origin and equate coefficients
a is l one l two, b is m one m two, two h is the cross sum
write the pair as a product of two general lines
pair ni product ga rasi coefficients equate cheyyali
match a b and two h

steps.why: Every proof in this chapter starts the same way: SPLIT the pair into its two separate lines with unknown coefficients, then match coefficients against the given equation. That dictionary between (a, h, b) and the two lines is what every later step spends.
common_mistakes: Using the slope form, which cannot handle a line with no y-term.
Writing 2h = l₁m₁ + l₂m₂ instead of the cross pairing.
steps.memory_tip: Split in the homogeneous form l₁x + m₁y — the form the distance formula expects.

steps.label: Write both perpendicular distances
steps.margin_note: One mark. Each line passes through the origin, so its equation has no constant — the perpendicular distance from (α, β) is just |l α + m β| over the root of the squares.
lines: Perpendicular distance from (α, β) to l₁x + m₁y = 0 is  p₁ = |l₁α + m₁β| / √(l₁² + m₁²)
Perpendicular distance from (α, β) to l₂x + m₂y = 0 is  p₂ = |l₂α + m₂β| / √(l₂² + m₂²)

recall.must_convey: That both perpendicular distances are written using |lα + mβ|/√(l² + m²).
accept: write the perpendicular distance from the point to each of the two lines
mod l alpha plus m beta over root l squared plus m squared
both lines pass through the origin so there is no constant term
rendu lines nunchi perpendicular distance rayali
both distances first
heard_as: root l squared plus m squared

steps.why: The lines pass through the origin, so c = 0 in the distance formula — which is what keeps both numerators to two terms.
common_mistakes: Including a constant term that is not there.
Putting α and β into the denominator.
steps.memory_tip: Each line passes through the origin, so there is no constant: the distance is |lα + mβ| over the root.

steps.label: Multiply them together
steps.margin_note: One mark. Multiply the two fractions, then multiply out both numerator and denominator so that everything is written in the products the dictionary knows.
lines: ∴ Product of perpendiculars is  p₁·p₂ = [|l₁α + m₁β| / √(l₁² + m₁²)] · [|l₂α + m₂β| / √(l₂² + m₂²)]
= |l₁l₂α² + l₁m₂αβ + l₂m₁αβ + m₁m₂β²| / √(l₁²l₂² + l₁²m₂² + l₂²m₁² + m₁²m₂²)

recall.must_convey: That multiplying and expanding gives |l₁l₂α² + (l₁m₂ + l₂m₁)αβ + m₁m₂β²| over the expanded root.
accept: multiply the two distances and expand both top and bottom
the numerator becomes l one l two alpha squared plus the cross terms plus m one m two beta squared
expand the product under the root as well
rendu multiply chesi expand cheyyali
multiply the two perpendicular distances

steps.why: The numerator's three groups are exactly a, 2h and b from the dictionary — that correspondence is the whole point of expanding rather than leaving it factored.
common_mistakes: Adding the two distances instead of multiplying.
Forgetting that the two middle terms combine into the 2h group.
steps.memory_tip: Multiply the two fractions and expand both parts into the products the dictionary knows.

steps.label: Convert to a, h, b
steps.margin_note: The last mark. The numerator substitutes directly. The denominator needs one rearrangement: add and subtract 2l₁l₂m₁m₂ so it becomes a difference of squares plus a square.

recall.must_convey: That substituting gives |aα² + 2hαβ + bβ²| over √((a − b)² + 4h²).
accept: substitute a b and two h into both the numerator and the denominator
the denominator becomes a minus b squared plus four h squared
the numerator is a alpha squared plus two h alpha beta plus b beta squared
a b two h substitute chesthe result vasthundi
this gives the required product

steps.why: The two extra terms added and subtracted cancel exactly, and what is left regroups as (a − b)² and (2h)² — which is why the answer's denominator has that shape.
common_mistakes: Forgetting the modulus on the numerator.
steps.memory_tip: Add and subtract 2l₁l₂m₁m₂ in the denominator so it becomes a difference of squares plus a square.

insider_note: Multiply the two distances, never add them, and keep both roots under one. The denominator regroups as (l₁l₂ − m₁m₂)² + (l₁m₂ + l₂m₁)² = (a − b)² + 4h²; writing (a + b)² there is the standard error.
